item.title: A Treasure Chest for (media) Pirates
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): Normal, but with "Notable Files" log.

Elevator Pitch: An anomaly where filesharing sites and FTP servers spontaneously obtain all pieces of media, even lost media with no evidence for its existence.

Central Narrative: Upon the first manifestation of the anomaly on ftp://[REDACTED], The Foundation, upon discovering mountains of classified material, and world governments, upon discovering mountains of illegal content, collaborate to shut down sites affected by SCP-XXXX. One server is archived by the Foundation, and contains the presumably infinite (yet 100TB in size) archive.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Notable content is recorded on a log by Information Researcher Jones. Throughout the logs, he documents his experiences and how his mental state is affected from seeing some of the more disturbing content in the archive.

Additional Notes: The concept of this is essentially "What if the Foundation was responsible for shutting down so many filesharing sites?".

item.title: Tale about the fall of the SCP Foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Elevator Pitch: The fall of the SCP Foundation is happening. Almost all of the SCPs have breached containment and are roaming the world. Site-[REDACTED] has almost been completely destroyed. The foundation is trying its best to re-contain all of the escaped SCPs

Central Narrative: One of the survivors of the site wide containment breach was a containment specialist, Victor. He was inside of the cafeteria eating his lunch when an unknown group broke into the site and freed almost all of the hostile SCPs. Victor escaped the site.

Now he has to survive in the most intense apocalypse known to mankind.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Its unique because Victor is dealing with many SCPs that have breached containment, and are possibly hostile. He has to survive a long and stressful time.

Additional Notes: I need help with the central narrative and the hook/attention grabber.

item.title: Dissociative Somnia Phenomenon
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight: YES

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator pitch:
An event in which an individual, usually that suffers from night terrors, will experience a dissociative episode(out of body experience) by "dreaming" about dying or killing. The dreams represent with precision the death of a person close to them, who will die within the next few weeks. Attempts to prevent this fate will often result in catastrophic outcomes.

Central Narrative:
The Inevitability of death and acceptance of loss.

Hook:
It's the classic "how would you react if you knew someone that you like is going to die?". I believe this concept to be interesting enough for the small intended size of the article.

Additional notes:
I'm not a hundred percent sure there isn't anything like this on the site already. I've looked around and found nothing that's close, but if there is, please, feel free to warn me.

item.title: The Most Annoying Fly You'll Ever Meet.
item.description: You know that fly that always seems to sneak its way into your room at night? Well, it can be much, much worse.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror with a tinge of dark comedy.

Page Layout (Optional): A standard SCP article included with experiences of D-Class dealing with the SCP and footnotes of some unusual instances of the SCP

Elevator Pitch: The first instance of SCP-??? is a small gnat that appears in the affected individual’s room anywhere from 10 P.M to 2 A.M and is first seen flying around a light source in the room or heard buzzing past the individual’s ear. This gnat proves extremely annoying, being nearly impossible to catch and contain for the night and will buzz by the individual’s ear just as they’re falling asleep. However, the gnat is very easy to kill, seemingly stopping if it’s approached with the intent of swatting it. But, killing the gnat will activate the next “stage” of SCP-???, this time a fly. Killing this instance again “ramps” up the SCP to a mosquito the next night, and so on and so on until you get mosquitoes with malaria, murder hornets, and other terrible crawlies. However, no matter what stage you’re on, they all follow the same rule of the insect being able to fly around and of being easy to kill but nearly impossible to catch and contain.

Central Narrative: I want to focus on how D-Class subjects either cope or go insane from this terrible predicament, and how bad it can get if you keep ramping up the stages.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A crawly in your rooms at night is something we’ve all dealt with at some point, so I feel like that familiar premise combined with my unique (hopefully) idea activates that deep fear of insects in the reader.

Additional Notes: I’m not positive if I want to have it ramp up to the point of being unbearable, or plateau at a certain point so it’s not enough to be completely devastating, but the annoyance is enough to slowly eat away at the individual. Curious on what your thoughts are.

item.title: Complete Desolation

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: A city thought to be destroyed by a tactical nuke is completely intact and functioning normally With one heat signature

Central Narrative: The heat signature is from a man that when researched can be found on file from [DATA REDACTED], Japan. He doesn’t seem aware that a nuke hit said city and lives in it agelessly

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The man has been shown to be talking to unknown people in the city in trivial conversation. It is unknown whether he is talking to an anomalous affect or is a schizophrenic. However when going to place of residence he shows signs of depression, possibly showing sapience to his situation.

Additional Notes: When the man goes to the edges of the city large tremors happen around him. It is unknown if him leaving will result in his neutralization. To counteract this he is forced by the foundation to stay in the inner area of the city until more information is found.

item.title: Of sirens and memetic agents
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Romance, History

Elevator Pitch: A siren that travels the world's seas in search of someone to marry. She exposes people to auditory and visual memetic agents that will make the exposed person fall in love with her; this usually ends with the siren accidentally drowning the exposed person. Any accurate depiction of her also carries this effect. However, the memes will only work on people who identify as a woman: people who identify as male will have a violent reaction to memes. The memes aren't distributed by artistic interpretations of her.

She first appeared in 1882; she was less of a problem then because she mostly isolated herself in the middle of the Atlantic ocean, not aware of the outside world. However, with the rise of mass media and the internet, she became more of a problem to secrecy as she began patrolling closer to large population centers and started placing advertisements carrying memetic agents on the internet through anomalous and non-anomalous means.

Central Narrative: The foundation originally discovered the siren in 1882, but due to her remote location, the foundation maneuvered ships away from her position and kept her mostly uncontained. The disappearance of Natalie Wood is the first real sign that the Siren has taken more provocative actions to secure a bride. The foundation can get a hold of her and does some interviews:

  • The first goes in-depth about her history: Her familial line is dying off and she was forced into marriage. However, due to her sexuality and her failing relationship with her husband, she ran away from home in search of another bride.
  • The second has the foundation propose an alternative; she can find a bride within the foundation staff as long as she stops advertising on the internet.
  • The third is a list of multiple proposed brides, equipped with memetic dampeners, and the siren's reaction to them. One of them gets selected, and some conversations are logged. It ends on a sweet tone, the siren finally having found someone who likes her back.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a wholesome article and this is mostly targeted at an audience that likes that, and it's pretty big. It also plays with the siren formula and introduces it to a modern setting. You could see it as a more family-friendly version of the original ''teenage succubus'' SCP.

item.title: SCP: Kingdom Come my first tale
item.description: The book of revelations with SCPs, inspired by DC's Kingdom Come
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

page type tale

genre: horror

page layout a transcript of a conversation with passages from the book revelations used as a framing device

Elevator pitch: Going off of what was established in the tale "new job". A former researcher on his death bed shares visions of an apocalyptic battle between SCP-999 and the scarlet king.

central narrative: while being read his last rites, the dying man interrupts the priest and starts yelling about his visions. The priest tries to tell him to save his strength, but the man insists he must listen. The visions begin with a great war between the SCP foundation and 6 other groups of interests, the war being about weather to destroy anomalies, study them, or let them be. The War comes to a head with an all out seige on site 19, where SCP-988 is being kept. During the battle, SCP-999 supposedly dies to save a researcher from SCP-049. That researcher then finds and opens SCP-988 The visions then skip ahead to the end of the seige, where SCP-053 and 682 are united and release some of the most dangerous SCPs. The survivors of the ensuing chaos come together despite their differences to try and stop this army of SCPs, and the Scarlet king feeds off the chaos of this battle. Pretty soon a portal to the scarlet king's world rips open and fire rains down as the Scarlet king enters our world. Just then SCP-999 reappears with a handful of other thaumiel class SCPs. Unfortunately the man dies before he can tell the man how it ends, but he does leave him with a warning not to "face the light when the day comes" before passing away.

hook: its an end of the world prediction that sorta lines up with the book of revelations.

item.title: The Hypnotic Spider
item.description: A tarantula that’s colors hypnotize any subject to view it. The subject will be compelled to let the tarantula eat it.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: People are horrified of spiders. This tarantula will grow depending on the amount it consumes. Since its anomalous effect is hypnotizing people to let it eat them, it can be a catastrophe if it ever gets loose.

Central Narrative: Will be about the spider itself and let the reader imagine the implications of the set of conditions for the SCP

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The spider is a Pamphobeteus sp. machala which has a beautifully purple carapace. It’s bright and to assume that looking at this spider will compel you to let it eat you.

Additional Notes: If this spider is ever let loose, it can grow to colossal size and be unstoppable if it finds enough food before teams are able to neutralize it.

item.title: The Blur *Seeking Greenlights*
item.description: an SCP article about a mysterious shadow
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is as the name suggest, a blur or as also seen as a shadow. It inhabits the very south of Argentina, the being is observed to have human level or higher intelligence and exhibits some anomalous abilities.

Central Narrative: This SCP is on close watch by the foundation, it having no physical body and only appearing as a semi transparent blur or a shadow makes it impossible to contain. So the foundation has decided to watch it via satellite. While it is not hostile towards anything, it has been observed to kill plant based life around it, likely by an unconscious ability to soak moisture from its surroundings. The foundation has no clear hypothesis for its existence but the most widely accepted one is that the SCP is an alternate dimensional being that exist on a semi 4 dimensional level, allowing it to have no physical body, yet still visible to 3 dimensional beings, although this theory is not proven.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP here has a lot of mystery around it, and I want to be able to not have a definitive answer what it exactly is. While the article will be mostly field notes by observers, I also want to explain why this SCP is as smart as a human and what ties it has to earth.

Additional Notes: I cant really explain everything here but if I can obtain 2 greenlights and make a sandbox, I can go into much better detail about this SCP and why it exist. Im not entirely sure where I can improve the central narrative to make it sound more interesting, but I have many ideas for this SCP so shoot your criticism at me so I can make this sound even more like a true SCP

item.title: SCP Idea: "The Answer Sheet"
item.description: A mind controlling piece of paper that is a portal to an alternate reality... but not really.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional): Regular SCP layout

Elevator Pitch: A regular looking piece of paper and an ink pen, that when written on using the aforementioned pen, grants a reply from the paper. The entity that replies through the paper is hyperintelligent, having knowledge of the O5 council and Level 5 clearance information that's withheld even from the researchers working on the SCP. It also has the ability to force anyone to grant any request that they read, which leads to many attempted escapes.

Central Narrative: A pair of entities, a pen and piece of paper, is discovered within an undisclosed SCP Site storage closet. After a junior researcher attempts to use the pen and paper together, he turns it in to his higher-ups, who begin experimentation on the entity. After discovering it's many abilities, such as it's incredible knowledge and it's way of making peopel complete requests, it is given strict safety and testing measures.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The way that the paper is very knowledagble about the Foundation, and how it can make people grant it's requests. It's a mysterious entity that much isn't known about, which leads to myriad tests on said entity.

Additional Notes: Looking especially for critique on how it makes people fufill the requests of readers, or if there's something that could work better with the idea.

item.title: Looking for critique on my SCP idea worked on it for a month now.

item.content:encoded:

SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
-A tree with galaxies as its canopy, the tree itself has multiple effects
(summary):

ones such as mass defects (cancer, deformations, etc)

began worshipping it

entrance directly transporting items or people to a depth of 83Km

from the tree (examples include)

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: in the 1600s the Conquistadors found the tree (in theorized adolescent age) and documented it before leaving back for a colony only for them to be killed by a cult who was at the time worshipping another god. After they found the tree they began to worship it and built a supermassive cathedral around it, the tree and cathedral were later discovered by SCP in the 1960s by SCP who confiscated the whole thing and imprisoned the Cult. item.title: The Abyss is Safe (seeking Crits and Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, and a narrative inter spliced with exploration logs and journal entries

Elevator Pitch: Life came from the cold, dark crushing depths of the sea, and that is where it is most safe, supposedly

Central Narrative: Talassaphobia is the fear of deep ocean, and is super common, but at the same time the ocean is considered to be the origin of all life. This SCP concept takes it to a new level: that beneath the deepest oceanic point on earth, the world is connected to a vast, interdimensional ocean. This ocean/SCP holds no deadly anomalies and living things entering this ocean go into a catatonic state and cannot be hurt or killed. The article would explore strange, normal animals that have entered and been affected by the space's effects, as well as exploration of the space itself. The main narrative doesn't exactly focus on it being this big inter dimensional space though, and is more about the small team of researchers that are for the most part left alone researching it. Along the ideas of “if you stare long enough into the abyss…” theming. While the main SCP may seem big, it is really more about how the people left alone with what would be consider a “safe” sort of anomaly do their best not to lose themselves in it, and what happens to the things that fail.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP takes a common fear and twists it into something welcoming. If you're familiar with the abyss from Dark Souls its similar: more of the pitch black being the true, calm nature of life and less so the rampaging monsters. It expires isolation, survival, and twisting the notion of what the deep ocean is like.

item.title: Murderous Power Cord

item.title: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious
item.description: At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image
item.content:encoded:
At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image in their heads: a bonsai tree sitting in some apartment in Iran.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Elevator Pitch: At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image in their heads: a bonsai tree sitting in an abandoned apartment in Iran.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation is compelled to visit an apartment that everybody, including other agencies concerned with the anomalous, seemed to know about. It turns out that the anomaly is not the apartment itself, but a bonsai tree sitting in the bedroom. The Foundation takes over the entire apartment complex, "managing" it to keep appearances. The apartment, officially the containment cell for the anomaly, looked to be lived in, but beyond writings and personal belongings of the tenant, there are no records of residence.

+ show block
– hide block

They find out that the bonsai tree emits radio signals through an invisible root system throughout the Earth. These radio signals cause those exposed to them for prolonged periods to feel intense dread and regret. Not much else learned about the bonsai tree, and the former tenant is still at large.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Knowledge of an object suddenly enters the collective unconscious.

Additional Notes: What I really want to highlight is the juxtaposition between the ubiquity of the bonsai tree within the collective unconscious and the anonymity of the original tenant. In summary, the tree is supposed to be representative of a universal dread, while the tenant, seemingly untrackable, is like an unobtainable goal.

While drafting this idea, I kept having trouble with suggesting the meaning of the tree's radio signals and the significance of the date in which it manifested. The idea is that the tree sort of feeds off of people's anxieties, and the "root system" connects to the minds of every person on Earth. The problem is that I don't want to be overt about it.

I'm not looking to write something scary or unsettling. I just want to make something that's curious.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Box of Miscellaneous Items

Elevator Pitch: Additional Notes: Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.I have an idea, but not sure how good it is so I want some advice. The skip is legit a cardboard box of random items. Every person swears the box is anomalous. But nothing happens, no sensor readings, no properties, nothing. It is, for all purposes, a random box with random goods inside. Just a plain old box. Yet, the Foundation- in all their wisdom and favor- cannot accept that they might have gotten one wrong. So its classified as either keter since the foundation starts associating random mundane everyday bad luck with it just to make some sense of it.

Pretty much, I want to tell this story of the Foundation being so zealous and confident that they cannot accept that they made a single mistake somewhere and have been wasting time on an ordinary box.

Central Narrative: Its going to describe the long and turtourus experience of many researchers attempting to prove that this box is anomalous. From scanners to shoving the box in with other skips, to eventual word of mouth fear of the box and its supposed properties. Eventually with high clearance the story will be shown that more and more tests came back negative, until only the O-5 council access shows it is a normal box but the council cannot admit it was a mistake.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I want to tell the story not of the Foundation being perfect, but rather as a flawed machine that thinks its perfect. Of thinking they cannot even make a single mistake.

item.title: A Canary In The Coal Mine
item.description: The story of researchers researching other researchers.
item.content:encoded:
The story of researchers researching other researchers. When the lines between 'tester' and 'testee' become blurred.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama

Page Layout (Optional): It will begin with a standard SCP article structure, followed by a series of experiment logs, journal extracts and Foundation documents explaining the story of the discovery of the subject.

Elevator Pitch: One day a researcher discovers a strange correlation between co-worker drinking a specific brand of soda and disasters/containment breaches occuring to their projects which he is certain is a viable "warning-light" to help contain dangerous SCPs.

Central Narrative: An anonomous researcher in one of the foundation sites has been secretly classified as a thaumiel class SCP, used as an early warning system for potential disasters that may befall foundation projects. Should this researcher drink a can of soda of a brand they typically claim to hate, it is a sign that a project which the researcher is assigned to will have a some form of disaster occur to it.

+ show block
– hide block

One observant co-worker, Dr. Gables, notices this trend and begins documenting it. What follows is a series of test logs and journal extracts of Dr. Gables investigating this anomouly and putting the paperwork in to give the researcher an official SCP designation. As the logs go on, experiments ramp up and start getting strange. By the time Dr. Gables has orchestrated an entire breach event resulting in multiple deaths, we realise that he had been operating without foundation clearance the entire time.

He uses an edited version of his obervations (with his involvment having been removed) to get the researcher an official SCP designation. Following a few more experiments, Dr. Gables goes insane and assaults the researcher. Following this, the Foundation investigates Dr. Gables to find his original observations that proved his involvement in multiple incidents, as well as numorous logs documenting other Foundation personnel and a large amount of blackmail which he has been using to get away with his actions. This concludes with a notice of termination of Dr. Gables and the reassignment of the SCP project to another researcher.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The dynamics of the relationships between Foundation researchers as well as the covert workings of a researcher with their own agendas and goals.

Additional Notes: I'm scared that readers may lose interest before getting to the meat of the story which would take place in the experiment logs and other attached documents.

item.title: Greenlight request- Frozen Corpse and Nervous System
item.description: First SCP attempt, with audio file attachment.
item.content:encoded:
I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror (body horror)

Page Layout (Optional): Class, containment procedures, description, addenda (including a voiceover mp3 file with sound effects)

Elevator Pitch: Pregnant woman is found frozen in the arctic, torn in half, fetus missing. Top half of body is dead, lower half moves erratically on its own, possibly with a purpose or cognition.

Central Narrative: Corpse was found frozen in Yukon when villagers noticed a strange, unidentified creature moving erratically. Corpse's lower half is controlled by a series of live neurons that consume the bone and ligament tissue and shock the muscles into moving convulsively, allowing it to crawl. It will violently hyperextend its joints (bending knees backwards and such) and break its own bones to move.

+ show block
– hide block

The live neuron DNA matches the dead woman, whose brain is somewhat shrunken, or possibly her fetus. Lead scientist believes it's capable of navigation and is searching for something, but regrets that its lifespan is so short as a result of consuming its own flesh and progressively deflating in size, that they'll never know what it wants. It must remain frozen to stay alive until the foundation finds a way to save it or find what it's looking for.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Using body horror as a focus, of which I haven't seen much here, and a full story with open-ended conclusion that is coherent with beginning, middle, and end if the reader reads between the lines. Specifically, I'd like to include a voiceover file from the scientist's observation session with written transcript, recording the skittering and cracking noises the skip makes, with a subtle hint/easter egg for readers to listen for, revealing what it's capable of, and possibly answering the question of what it actually wants (this won't be included in the transcript, so that the reader is left to think and interpret it on their own).

Additional Notes: Please advise how to include the mp3 file with submission, as it's essential to the storytelling, thanks.

Central Narrative: The Foundation is in the process of investigating and researching this anomaly, but really no true containment is deemed necessary… so far. Researchers front as locals or vacationers to try and sneak past the defensive isolated population. Posing as an environmental group, they interview and interrogate locals on the appearance and disappearance of these fountains.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The memetic effects on the locals cause paranoia, defensiveness, and a stubborn attitude in regards to the fountains. This will be expanded upon in the interview logs, which I plan to have make up a lot of the page. Don't want to give TOO much away.

Additional Notes: I have already written a pretty in depth draft, just excluding the interview logs. Feel free to ask any questions, or to see the sandbox page.
